issue_context.title: posix: getopt: Compile warnings with getopt_long
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
After the changes by https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/48130, lib/posix/getopt/getopt_long.c will compile with a warning that "char* dash_prefix" may be uninitialized before use in function "parse_long_options".

While the root concern of this warning will never happen on runtime due to conditional checks, the compiler is conservative and throws the warning never the less, causing problems if the use of this file is to be combined with the -Werror compile flag.

**To Reproduce**
- Set up a blank project for nRF5340
- Include getopt and call the parse_long_options function at least once in the source code
- Build using west build, and make sure to include -Werror as a compile flag:
- west build -p -b nrf5340_audio_dk_nrf5340_cpuapp -d build_output_folder -- -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS="-Werror"

**Expected behavior**
Build should be successful

**Impact**
Any project using a strict no-build-warning policy is unable to use getopt_long.c.

**Environment:**
OS: Linux
Toolchain Zephyr SDK 0.15.2
Zephyr 3.3.99

**Additional context**
Possible solutions include to initialize this variable in the case it is not used, as was the case in the past, or do the conditional checks associated with it on compile-time instead of runtime.
comments: @Frodevan - can you please use the bug template for your summary?
@Frodevan - is there a `west` repro command that you can add to the summary?

@Frodevan - can you provide a repro command that can be run in the zephyr repository by an arbitrary person who does not have access to your source code?

We should be able to see the warning against an existing (in-tree) Zephyr app - perhaps something of the format

```
west build -b board -t run samples/...
west build -b board -t run tests/...
```

@cfriedt ok, you should be able to do the following, assuming you have the Zephyr toolchain all set up and ready:

**step 1: Fetch code to be compiled**
- Make an empty directory and open a command line interface there. (Note: Make sure to **_not_** have a space in the filepath of this directory.)
- Run the following commands:
```
git clone https://github.com/koffes/sdk-nrf.git nrf
cd nrf
git checkout bis_acl_test
cd ..
```

**Step 2: Make sure zephyrptoject-rtos Zephyr and not the downstream fork is used**
- In the file **nrf/west.yml**, replace what's on line 61 and 62 with the following and save:
_Line 61:_ `      url: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr.git`
_Line 62:_ `      revision: main`

**Step 3: Prepare and invoke build**
- In the cli (same folder as before), run:
```
west init -l nrf
west update
```
- Wait for everything to fetch, it takes a few minutes
- Copy this one file from the downstream fork into the **zephyr/modules/mbedtls** folder: https://github.com/nrfconnect/sdk-zephyr/blob/main/modules/mbedtls/Kconfig.psa. This is unrelevant to the bug, but the code we will compile needs it.
- In the cli:
```
west build -p -b nrf5340_audio_dk_nrf5340_cpuapp -d build_output_folder nrf/tests/bluetooth/iso -- -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS="-Werror"
```

**Step 4: Observe**
- fatal error since all warnings being treated as errors

As of samples in Zephyr itself, I was not able to find any that sets the CONFIG_GETOPT_LONG flag. If you compile any other sample (for example samples/bluetooth/hci_uart or something like that) for this target with **-DCONFIG_GETOPT=y -DCONFIG_GETOPT_LONG=y -DCONFIG_SHELL_GETOPT=y** added to the end of the build-command, it should in theory invoke the bug.

If you run this build-command, it will invoke the bug:
`west build -p -b nrf5340_audio_dk_nrf5340_cpuapp -d build zephyr/samples/bluetooth/iso_broadcast/ -- -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS="-Werror" -DCONFIG_GETOPT=y -DCONFIG_GETOPT_LONG=y`

One note, there are no samples in Zephyr for this target that enable the CONFIG_GETOPT_LONG flag by default, which is why it has to be manually selected here.

@Frodevan - probably a better repro recipe is here. And it seems we actually do have coverage for `CONFIG_GETOPT_LONG`. This would be executed in CI pretty regularly.
```
twister -i --build-only -p nrf5340_audio_dk_nrf5340_cpuapp -T tests/posix/getopt
# or the command below for 
west build -p always -b nrf5340_audio_dk_nrf5340_cpuapp tests/posix/getopt -- -DCONFIG_COMPILER_WARNINGS_AS_ERRORS=y
```

If you don't mind, please try to use the common formats above for reproducibility information next time. I do appreciate the bug report though - thank you!

What I find weird is this: normally, `twister` has historically elevated all (most?) warnings to errors and we have some Kconfig options that imply `-Werror` is enabled.

There are a few layers of abstraction here, and sorry for the safari, but `twister` normally [sets](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/main/scripts/pylib/twister/twisterlib/runner.py#L328) `CONFIG_COMPILER_WARNINGS_AS_ERRORS=y`.

Then, in `CMakeLists.txt`, we have `zephyr_compile_options($<$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:C>:$<TARGET_PROPERTY:compiler,warnings_as_errors>>)`. which translates to the following based on the toolchain:
```shell
~/zephyrproject/zephyr (main)]$ grep -R "warnings_as_errors" cmake/
cmake/compiler/arcmwdt/compiler_flags.cmake:set_property(TARGET compiler PROPERTY warnings_as_errors -Werror)
cmake/compiler/arcmwdt/compiler_flags.cmake:set_property(TARGET asm PROPERTY warnings_as_errors -Werror)
cmake/compiler/gcc/compiler_flags.cmake:set_property(TARGET compiler PROPERTY warnings_as_errors -Werror)
cmake/compiler/gcc/compiler_flags.cmake:set_property(TARGET asm PROPERTY warnings_as_errors -Werror -Wa,--fatal-warnings)
cmake/compiler/compiler_flags_template.cmake:set_property(TARGET compiler PROPERTY warnings_as_errors)
cmake/compiler/compiler_flags_template.cmake:set_property(TARGET asm PROPERTY warnings_as_errors)
cmake/linker/arcmwdt/linker_flags.cmake:set_property(TARGET linker PROPERTY warnings_as_errors -Wl,--fatal-warnings)
cmake/linker/ld/gcc/linker_flags.cmake:set_property(TARGET linker PROPERTY warnings_as_errors -Wl,--fatal-warnings)
cmake/linker/linker_flags_template.cmake:set_property(TARGET linker PROPERTY warnings_as_errors)
```

Just to verify that all of the above works as expected, I used [this suggestion from the docs](https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/develop/west/build-flash-debug.html#verbose-builds).

```shell
ccache .../arm-zephyr-eabi-gcc \
   ... \
  -Werror \
  -Wall \
  -Wformat \
  -Wformat-security \
  -Wno-format-zero-length \
  -Wno-pointer-sign \
  -Wpointer-arith \
  -Wexpansion-to-defined \
  -Wno-unused-but-set-variable \
  -Werror=implicit-int \
  ... \
  -c .../getopt/getopt_long.c
```

With that, it's clear that `-Werror` is set.
I'll leave the bug label for now. If you can provide any additional information, that would be great.

> west build -p -b nrf5340_audio_dk_nrf5340_cpuapp -d build zephyr/samples/bluetooth/iso_broadcast/ -- -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS="-Werror" -DCONFIG_GETOPT=y -DCONFIG_GETOPT_LONG=y

@koffes just saw this.

Was able to reproduce with a slightly different command
```shell
west build \
    -b nrf5340_audio_dk_nrf5340_cpuapp \
    samples/bluetooth/iso_broadcast/ \
    -- \
    -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS="-Werror" \
    -DCONFIG_GETOPT=y \
    -DCONFIG_GETOPT_LONG=y
```
as well as this one, which more closely represents what would be run in CI
```
west build \
    -b nrf5340_audio_dk_nrf5340_cpuapp \
    samples/bluetooth/iso_broadcast/ \
    -- \
    -DCONFIG_COMPILER_WARNINGS_AS_ERRORS=y \
    -DCONFIG_GETOPT=y \
    -DCONFIG_GETOPT_LONG=y
```

So I'll merge the fix. However, I need to investigate why `twister` does not seem to be escalating the `-Werror` at some point, or there is some other issue with the testsuite.

@jakub-uC are you able to investigate why `tests/posix/getopt` passes in CI in spite of the uninitialized `current_dash` variable? For some reason, I'm actually unable to make the testsuite fail. It's possible that there is some aspect of `samples/bluetooth/iso_broadcast` that triggers an uncovered code path in the getopt code.

I guess that should probably be part of a new ticket.

> @cfriedt 
> 
> Variable `current_dash` is used only for logging purposes. For the sake of saving memory and to be able to run the test on as many platforms as possible, the logger module was disabled in this test. Since the logger is disabled then the code where `current_dash` is used does not compile at all.
> As a result, the `tests/posix/getopt` test does not generate a warning.

@jakub-uC - would it be possible to add a new permutation to `testcase.yaml` that enables the logger with a min ram filter?
